summary_paragraph: John, a homeless man with a history of hypertension and alcohol abuse, was admitted after a fall following heavy alcohol consumption. He was found to be in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, likely due to noncompliance with his previous metoprolol regimen. His heart rate was poorly controlled with beta-blockers but responded to diltiazem, which was started in the hospital and continued at discharge. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or shoulder injuries, and chest pain was deemed musculoskeletal. He showed no signs of alcohol withdrawal and received supportive supplementation with thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. He was discharged home with medication adherence counseling, new prescriptions, and follow-up arranged with community health services.
